exercises.heading: 2.5. Exercises

problem.paragraph: Write an equation that expresses the fact that a function $$f$$ is continuous at the number $$4$$ .
If $$f$$ is continuous on $$\left( {- \infty,\infty} \right)$$ , what can you say about its graph?

list.item: From the given graph of $$f$$ , state the numbers at which $$f$$ is discontinuous and explain why.

For each of the numbers stated in part (a), determine whether $$f$$ is continuous from the right, or from the left, or neither. Details A function with four parts is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The x axis is displayed from below negative 4 to beyond 6 in increments of 2 units. The first part enters the second quadrant above the x axis at approximately x = negative 5, goes up and to the right through the open dot which is plotted at x = negative 4, concave down, and ends with a solid dot at x = negative 2. The second part begins with an open dot at x = negative 2, directly across the open dot of the first part, goes linearly upward to the right until it reaches the positive y axis, then goes down and to the right, concave up, and ends with an open dot at x = 2, just above the x axis. The third part begins in the first quadrant at x = 2 with a solid dot, far away from the x axis, goes down and to the right, concave down, and crosses the x axis at (3.5, 0). The fourth part begins in the first quadrant at x = 4 with a solid dot, a little above the x axis, goes down and to the right, concave up, veering toward the x axis, exiting very close to it.
$$- 4$$ , $$- 2$$ , $$2$$ , $$4$$ ; $$f\left( {- 4} \right)$$ is not defined and $$\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow a}f(x)$$ does not exist for $$a = - 2$$ , $$2$$ , and $$4$$
$$- 4$$ , neither; $$- 2$$ , left; 2, right; 4, right

problem.paragraph: From the given graph of $$g$$ , state the numbers at which $$g$$ is discontinuous and explain why.

image.alt: Details A function with four parts is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The x axis is displayed from negative 3 to 3 in increments of 1 unit. The first part begins with a solid dot at x = negative 3 in the second quadrant, goes down and to the right through the open dot which is plotted at x = negative 2, concave down, crosses the x axis at approximately (negative 1.4, 0), veering towards x = negative 1 in the third quadrant as it steeply falls downward. The second part enters from the bottom of the third quadrant to the right of x = negative 1, goes up and to the right, concave down, crosses the x axis at approximately (negative 0.6, 0), and ends on the positive y axis with a solid dot. The third part begins with an open dot on the negative y axis, goes down and to the right, concave down, and ends with an open dot at x = 1. There is a solid dot at x = 1 in the fourth quadrant, directly across the open dot of the previous part. The fourth part begins with an open dot at x = 1, above the positive x axis, goes up and to the right, concave up, and ends with a solid dot at x = 3.

exercises.instruction: 5–6 The graph of a function $$f$$ is given. At what numbers $$a$$ does $$\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow a}f(x)$$ not exist? At what numbers $$a$$ is $$f$$ not continuous? At what numbers $$a$$ does $$\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow a}f(x)$$ exist but $$a$$ is not continuous at $$a$$ ?

problem.paragraph: 5. Details A function with two parts is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The x axis is displayed from negative 1 to 5 in increments of 1 unit. The first part enters the second quadrant, runs horizontally to the right, and ends with an open dot in the first quadrant at x = 1. The second part begins with a solid dot at x = 1, directly below the open dot of the first part, goes linearly upward to the right, and reaches an open dot at x = 3. It then falls linearly to the right until approximately x = 4.5, and runs horizontally rightward. Below the second part, there is a solid dot at x = 3 directly across the open dot of the first part. $$1$$ $$1$$ , $$3$$ $$3$$

6. Details A function with three parts is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The x axis is displayed from negative 1 to 5 in increments of 1 unit. The first part of the curve enters the second quadrant above the x axis, goes up and to the right, concave up, crosses the positive y axis, enters into the first quadrant, and exits the viewing window very close to the left of x = 1 at the top. A solid dot is plotted at x = 1 above the x axis. The second part enters the first quadrant at the top, very close to the right of x = 1, goes down and to the right, concave up, reaches x = 3 with an open dot, then rises linearly to the right and ends with a solid dot at x = 5 above the x axis. Another solid dot is plotted at x = 3 directly above the open dot of the second part. The third part begins with an open dot at x = 5, directly above the solid dot of the second part, and runs horizontally rightward.

exercises.instruction: 7, 8, 9, and 10 Sketch the graph of a function $$f$$ that is defined on $$\mathbb{R}$$ and continuous except for the stated discontinuities.

problem.paragraph: Removable discontinuity at $$- 2$$ , infinite discontinuity at $$2$$
Jump discontinuity at $$- 3$$ , removable discontinuity at $$4$$
Discontinuities at $$0$$ and $$3$$ , but continuous from the right at $$0$$ and from the left at $$3$$
Continuous only from the left at $$- 1$$ , not continuous from the left or right at $$3$$
The toll $$T$$ charged for driving on a certain stretch of a toll road is $$\$ 5$$ except during rush hours (between 7 am and 10 am and between 4 pm and 7 pm) when the toll is $$\$ 7$$ .

list.item: Sketch a graph of $$T$$ as a function of the time $$t$$ , measured in hours past midnight.
Discuss the discontinuities of this function and their significance to someone who uses the road.

problem.paragraph: Explain why each function is continuous or discontinuous.

list.item: The temperature at a specific location as a function of time
The temperature at a specific time as a function of the distance due west from New York City
The altitude above sea level as a function of the distance due west from New York City
The cost of a taxi ride as a function of the distance traveled
The current in the circuit for the lights in a room as a function of time

27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 33, and 34 Explain, using Theorems 4, 5, 7, and 9, why the function is continuous at every number in its domain. State the domain.

39–40 Locate the discontinuities of the function and illustrate by graphing.
43, 44, and 45 Find the numbers at which $$f$$ is discontinuous. At which of these numbers is $$f$$ continuous from the right, from the left, or neither? Sketch the graph of $$f$$ .

where $$M$$ is the mass of Earth, $$R$$ is its radius, and $$G$$ is the gravitational constant. Is $$F$$ a continuous function of $$r$$ ?
For what value of the constant $$c$$ is the function $$f$$ continuous on $$\left( {- \infty,\infty} \right)$$ ?
Find the values of $$a$$ and $$b$$ that make $$f$$ continuous everywhere.
Suppose $$f$$ and $$g$$ are continuous functions such that $$g(2) = 6$$ and $$\lim_{x\rightarrow 2}\left\lbrack {3f(x) + f(x)g(x)} \right\rbrack = 36$$ . Find $$f(2)$$ .

list.item: Find $$\left( {f \circ g} \right)(x)$$ .
Is $$f \circ g$$ continuous everywhere? Explain.

problem.paragraph: Which of the following functions $$f$$ has a removable discontinuity at $$a$$ ? If the discontinuity is removable, find a function $$g$$ that agrees with $$f$$ for $$x \neq a$$ and is continuous at $$a$$ .

Suppose that a function $$f$$ is continuous on $$\lbrack 0,1\rbrack$$ except at $$0.25$$ and that $$f(0) = 1$$ and $$f(1) = 3$$ . Let $$N = 2$$ . Sketch two possible graphs of $$f$$ , one showing that $$f$$ might not satisfy the conclusion of the Intermediate Value Theorem and one showing that $$f$$ might still satisfy the conclusion of the Intermediate Value Theorem (even though it doesn’t satisfy the hypothesis).
If $$f(x) = x^{2} + 10\sin x$$ , show that there is a number $$c$$ such that $$f(c) = 1000$$ .
Suppose $$f$$ is continuous on $$\lbrack 1,5\rbrack$$ and the only solutions of the equation $$f(x) = 6$$ are $$x = 1$$ and $$x = 4$$ . If $$f(2) = 8$$ , explain why $$f(3) > 6$$ .

exercises.instruction: 55, 56, 57, and 58 Use the Intermediate Value Theorem to show that there is a solution of the given equation in the specified interval.
59–60 Prove that the equation has at least one real solution. Use a calculator to find an interval of length $$0.01$$ that contains a solution.
61–62 Prove that the equation has at least one real solution. Find the solution correct to three decimal places, by graphing.
63–64 Prove, without graphing, that the graph of the function has at least two $$x$$ -intercepts in the specified interval.

A Tibetan monk leaves the monastery at 7:00 am and takes his usual path to the top of the mountain, arriving at 7:00 pm. The following morning, he starts at 7:00 am at the top and takes the same path back, arriving at the monastery at 7:00 pm. Use the Intermediate Value Theorem to show that there is a point on the path that the monk will cross at exactly the same time of day on both days.
